summary.text: A 22-year-old black male with a two year history of recurrent maculopapular rashes and occasional joint pains, treated with methotrexate, steroids and hydroxychloroquine under dermatology suspicion of SLE, presented to the emergency unit with two weeks of bilateral pedal edema, oliguria, haematuria, abdominal distension and scrotal swelling and a single generalized tonic-clonic seizure. He was pale, afebrile, hypertensive at 156/100mmHg with a malar rash, basal crackles and a left stony dull percussion note.

Admission hemoglobin was 7.4g/dl, urea 23.7mmol/L and creatinine 256umol/L, rising to a peak of 433μmol/L, with hypercholesterolemia, hypoalbuminemia, dipstick protein ++++ and UPCR 6.29 g/day. ANA was positive at 1/160, anti-Smith antibody exceeded 480U/ml and anti-dsDNA was negative. Ultrasound showed enlarged echogenic kidneys, ascites and a left pleural effusion. Ultrasound-guided renal biopsy histology was suggestive of class IV lupus nephritis with elements of class V.

Hypertension was managed with furosemide, nifedipine and carvedilol, and one unit of blood was transfused. He continued prednisolone 60mg/day and mycophenolate mofetil 1.5g twice a day, with creatinine falling to 95umol/L and albumin rising to 36g/L after six months. Complications included acne, steroid induced dyspepsia, ESBL Enterobacter aerogenes urinary tract infection treated with parenteral amikacin, oropharyngeal candidiasis treated with fluconazole, and herpes zoster ophthalmicus treated with acyclovir; immunosuppression was reduced and UPCR rose to 9.7g/day. Post herpetic neuralgia responded to amitriptyline.
He is followed at the renal clinic and is in partial remission with proteinuria improved to 0.55g/day and no new medication complication on maintenance therapy.
